issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֶל תַּחַת הָאֵלָה' means 'to under the oak' (i.e., under the terebinth/oak tree), but the Chinese renders it as '帶到以拉人那裡' ('brought to the Elah people'), misinterpreting the place name/word 'הָאֵלָה' (the oak/terebinth) as a people group '以拉人'. This changes the location from a tree to a group of people.
